title: Timothy: without repetition or sequence the listener is lost
summary: He repeats Timothy's lesson and compares music to a rambling speaker.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: I asked Timothy one time, "What's the most important thing in music?" He said, "Without repetition or sequence, the listener don't understand what you're doing." So music.... You listen to all the symphonies. It's a matter of repetition or sequence. Now, sequence is the same thing on a different level.
Yeah. But it's the same thing. And it's just like a guy talking...

He said, "Without sequence or repetition (he says you use both], the listener don't understand what you were playing." And I adapt the music to speech. If you've got a guy that's getting up talking, and he just rambles from one thought to another, you don't understand what he was saying.
So in conclusion, you're saying if a guy just rambles like that...
